items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: because Frank Loesser was a personal friend of Barney Josephson's

ctx.x: Well, I can't remember. All I know, whatever was considered the amount to make it a hit. That's what happened. And it happened quickly, you know. And what was so amazing is the fact that the records of course are released -- were, I guess they still are -- were released in New York before they were released here. And when I was

approached by Barney Josephson to go to Cafe Society, who was the big thing, you know, he was the big man and Cafe Society was the most popular spot in New York at that time -- this was 1947 -- and when he heard this record, my record, I think he was -- he was very carried away because Frank Loesser was a personal friend of Barney Josephson's, and I don't know -- he heard it at somebody's house or heard something, but he knew it was a Loesser tune, and then he liked both sides of it, and he became very…

got to go to New York. They want you to go to New York. Barney is coming out here to talk to me about you going to New York." I said, "Oh, really?" He said, "Yes." So anyway, I told him when I would be home, and when I came he said, well, you've got to come down and see Barney. We'll get together with him. So I met Barney Josephson, and he was very, very, very interested in my coming to New York. He said, "You've got to come to New York. You've just got to." Well, I don't know, it just didn't hit me, as I said…
